items.title: Centre of mass, the identity $\sum_i m_i\rho_i=0$, and the splitting of the kinetic sum $\sum_i m_i\lVert x_i'\rVert_2^2$ into centre-of-mass and relative parts (with the two-body reduced-mass case)
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb N$, $N\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two points ([[def-interval]]), let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ and let $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be differentiable at every point of $I$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). All sums over $i$ range over $1,\dots,N$: for a real family $a_1,\dots,a_N$, define $\sum_i a_i:=\sum_{k<N}b_k$, where $b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ has $b_k=a_{k+1}$ for $k<N$ and $b_k=0$ for $k\ge N$, using the finite sums of [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]; vector sums are defined coordinatewise, and sums of curves pointwise. Put $M:=\sum_i m_i>0$, $X:=M^{-1}\sum_i m_ix_i$ and $\rho_i:=x_i-X$. The symbols $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ and $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ denote the Euclidean inner product and norm on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then:

1. $X$ and every $\rho_i$ are differentiable on $I$, with $X'=M^{-1}\sum_im_ix_i'$ and $\rho_i'=x_i'-X'$, and the identities $\sum_im_i\rho_i=0$ and $\sum_im_i\rho_i'=0$ hold on $I$;
2. for every $t\in I$, $$\sum_{i}m_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=M\lVert X'(t)\rVert_2^2+\sum_{i}m_i\lVert\rho_i'(t)\rVert_2^2;$$
3. if $N=2$, then with $r:=x_1-x_2$ and $\mu:=m_1m_2/M$ one has $\sum_im_i\lVert\rho_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_2^2$ and hence $$\sum_{i}m_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=M\lVert X'(t)\rVert_2^2+\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_2^2$$ for every $t\in I$.
items.strategy: Differentiate the defining finite sums; differentiate the zero identity; expand the squared norm by bilinearity with the cross term killed by sum m_i rho_i'=0; specialise rho_1=(m_2/M)r, rho_2=-(m_1/M)r.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §1.3, Eqs. (1.15)-(1.16) and (1.22)-(1.23), printed pp. 6-8: the centre of mass and the kinetic-energy split
Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics, §3.4, Eqs. (3.30)-(3.35), printed pp. 40-42: centre of mass and reduced mass for two bodies

items.title: Total momentum and total angular momentum balances for a finite system with antisymmetric pair forces; pairwise central forces make the internal torque vanish
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two points ([[def-interval]]), let $N\ge1$, let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$, and let $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be twice differentiable, i.e. differentiable with derivative $x_i'$ differentiable ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Write $p_i:=m_ix_i'$ and suppose there are maps $f_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ and, for every ordered pair $i\ne j$ in $\{1,\dots,N\}$, maps $f_{ij}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ such that

$$f_{ij}(t)=-f_{ji}(t),\qquad p_i'(t)=f_i(t)+\sum_{j\ne i}f_{ij}(t)\qquad(t\in I).$$

Write $P:=\sum_ip_i$, $J:=\sum_ix_i\times p_i$ (cross product in $\mathbb R^3$, [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Then:

1. $P$ is differentiable on $I$ with $P'(t)=\sum_if_i(t)$ for all $t\in I$;
2. $J$ is differentiable on $I$ with $$J'(t)=\sum_ix_i(t)\times f_i(t)+\sum_{i<j}\bigl(x_i(t)-x_j(t)\bigr)\times f_{ij}(t)\qquad(t\in I);$$
3. if in addition, for every $i<j$, $f_{ij}$ is parallel to $x_i-x_j$ — that is, there is a real function $\lambda_{ij}$ on $I$ with $f_{ij}=\lambda_{ij}(x_i-x_j)$ — then $J'(t)=\sum_ix_i(t)\times f_i(t)$ for all $t\in I$.
items.strategy: Sum the balance equations; differentiate each cross product, kill x_i' x p_i by alternation, and reindex the internal double sum using antisymmetry; parallel pairs have vanishing (x_i-x_j) x f_ij.

Richard Fitzpatrick, Classical Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin), Non-Isolated Systems, Eqs. (41)-(44): external momentum and torque balances with internal cancellation

items.title: Work-energy balance $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(K+U(t,x(t))\bigr)=\partial_tU(t,x(t))+\sum_i\langle d_i(t),x_i'(t)\rangle$ for forces $m_ix_i''=-\nabla_{x_i}U+d_i$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two points ([[def-interval]]), let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ be nonempty and open, and let $U:I\times Q\to\mathbb R$ be the restriction of a function $\widehat U:J\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$, where $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open interval containing $I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Write points of $Q$ as $q=(q_1,\dots,q_N)$ with $q_i\in\mathbb R^3$; for $t\in I$, $q\in Q$ and each $i$ let $\nabla_{x_i}U(t,q)\in\mathbb R^3$ be the gradient of $u\mapsto U(t,q_1,\dots,q_{i-1},u,q_{i+1},\dots,q_N)$ at $u=q_i$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), and let $\partial_tU$ and the spatial derivatives on $I\times Q$ denote the derivatives of $\widehat U$ restricted there. At an included endpoint of $I$, derivatives of curves are limits relative to $I$ (one-sided there); this preserves closed and half-open time intervals. Let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$, let $x:I\to Q$ be twice differentiable ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), put $K(t):=\frac12\sum_im_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2$ (Euclidean norm, [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), let $d_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be maps, and suppose

$$m_ix_i''(t)=-\nabla_{x_i}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+d_i(t)\qquad(t\in I,\ 1\le i\le N).$$

Then:

1. $K$ is differentiable on $I$ with $K'(t)=\sum_i\langle m_ix_i''(t),x_i'(t)\rangle$;
2. $t\mapsto U(t,x(t))$ is differentiable on $I$ with $$\frac{d}{dt}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)=\partial_tU\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_i\bigl\langle\nabla_{x_i}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr),x_i'(t)\bigr\rangle;$$
3. consequently $$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(K(t)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\Bigr)=\partial_tU\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)+\sum_i\langle d_i(t),x_i'(t)\rangle\qquad(t\in I);$$ in particular, if $d_i\equiv0$ for all $i$ then $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(K+U(t,x(t))\bigr)=\partial_tU(t,x(t))$, and if in addition $\partial_tU\equiv0$ then $t\mapsto K(t)+U(t,x(t))$ is constant on $I$.
items.strategy: Differentiate the squared norms; apply the chain rule to the composite U(t,x(t)) and read the total derivative on (1,x'(t)) through the Jacobian; add and substitute the force identity; conclude constancy by the zero-derivative criterion.

items.title: Variable-mass momentum balance: from $m'=r_{\rm in}-r_{\rm out}$ and $(mv)'=F+r_{\rm in}w_{\rm in}-r_{\rm out}w_{\rm out}$ to $mv'=F+r_{\rm in}(w_{\rm in}-v)-r_{\rm out}(w_{\rm out}-v)$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), let $m:I\to(0,\infty)$ and $v:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be differentiable ([[def-derivative]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), and let $F:I\to\mathbb R^3$, $r_{\mathrm{in}},r_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to[0,\infty)$ and $w_{\mathrm{in}},w_{\mathrm{out}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be maps. Suppose the two **material balance identities**

$$m'(t)=r_{\mathrm{in}}(t)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(t),\qquad (mv)'(t)=F(t)+r_{\mathrm{in}}(t)w_{\mathrm{in}}(t)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(t)w_{\mathrm{out}}(t)$$

hold for every $t\in I$, where $mv$ denotes the pointwise scalar multiple. Then

$$m(t)v'(t)=F(t)+r_{\mathrm{in}}(t)\bigl(w_{\mathrm{in}}(t)-v(t)\bigr)-r_{\mathrm{out}}(t)\bigl(w_{\mathrm{out}}(t)-v(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in I).$$

In particular, if $F\equiv0$, $r_{\mathrm{in}}\equiv0$ and $r_{\mathrm{out}}\equiv r$ for a constant $r\ge0$, then $mv'=-r(w_{\mathrm{out}}-v)$: the acceleration is governed by the momentum carried away per unit time relative to the body, not by $(mv)'=0$.

The two balance identities are the **adopted content of the material momentum accounting** — the mathematical rendering of "gains $r_{\mathrm{in}}\,dt$ of matter with velocity $w_{\mathrm{in}}$, loses $r_{\mathrm{out}}\,dt$ with velocity $w_{\mathrm{out}}$, and feels the external force $F$". They are not derived here from any closed-system law; the deduction below is their product-rule consequence.
items.strategy: Product rule coordinatewise for (mv)', substitute the mass-rate identity, and group the flux terms.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §1.2, printed p. 2: the momentum form $\mathbf F=\dot{\mathbf p}$ for a body of varying mass, with the warning that the closed-system statement needs open-system momentum accounting

Richard Fitzpatrick, Classical Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin), Non-Isolated Systems: the total-momentum balance $d\mathbf P/dt=\mathbf F$ with external force, the form that fails to track ejected/absorbed material without the flux terms below

items.title: Compact continuation for locally Lipschitz ODEs: a solution whose graph stays in a compact subset of the domain near a finite endpoint extends past it
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open, and let $F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable, locally uniformly in time, in the sense of [[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]. Let $t_0<b$ be reals, let $x_0\in\mathbb R^n$ with $(t_0,x_0)\in D$, and let $x:[t_0,b)\to\mathbb R^n$ be a solution of the initial value problem

$$x'(t)=F\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr),\qquad x(t_0)=x_0$$

on $[t_0,b)$ ([[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]). Suppose there is a compact set $K\subseteq D$ and a real $\delta>0$ such that

$$\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\in K\qquad\text{for every }t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap[t_0,b).$$

Then:

1. there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a solution $\tilde x:[t_0,b+\varepsilon)\to\mathbb R^n$ of the same initial value problem with $\tilde x(t)=x(t)$ for all $t\in[t_0,b)$; in particular $\tilde x(b)=\lim_{t\uparrow b}x(t)$ exists and lies in the state projection of $K$;
2. if moreover $D=\mathbb R\times U$ for an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $F$ is autonomous, $F(t,z)=G(z)$ with $G:U\to\mathbb R^n$ continuous and locally Lipschitz in the state variable ([[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]), and if there is a compact $K_0\subseteq U$ with $x(t)\in K_0$ for every $t\in(b-\delta,b)\cap[t_0,b)$, then the extension conclusion of clause 1 holds as well.
items.strategy: Bound F on K, get a Lipschitz estimate from the Volterra equation, produce the one-sided limit x_b by completeness, place (b,x_b) in the closed K, apply Picard-Lindelof at (b,x_b), and glue by uniqueness; clause 2 repeats the argument with K0.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, §2.6 Extensibility of solutions, printed pp. 50-53: gluing, Corollary 2.15 (compact continuation) and Corollary 2.16 (escape of every compact set)
Julien Arino, MATH 8430 Fundamental Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations (University of Manitoba), §1.3 Continuation of solutions, printed pp. 24-28: Lemma 1.3.1, Theorem 1.3.3 and Theorem 1.3.7

items.title: The distributional derivative of a piecewise $C^1$ function with a jump: $(u_p)'=u_{p'_{\mathrm{reg}}}+[p]\,\delta_{t_*}$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes; declares AC_omega for the Lebesgue distribution suppliers
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), used only through the Borel-measurability, Lebesgue-integration and distribution suppliers cited below. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval ([[def-interval]]), let $t_*\in I$, and let $p:I\to\mathbb R$ satisfy:

1. $p$ is continuous on $I\setminus\{t_*\}$ and of class $C^1$ on each of the two open intervals $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,\infty)$;
2. the one-sided limits $p(t_*^-):=\lim_{t\uparrow t_*}p(t)$, $p(t_*^+):=\lim_{t\downarrow t_*}p(t)$ and the one-sided limits of the derivative $p'(t_*^-):=\lim_{t\uparrow t_*}p'(t)$, $p'(t_*^+):=\lim_{t\downarrow t_*}p'(t)$ all exist in $\mathbb R$.

Fix a value $p(t_*)\in\mathbb R$ arbitrarily (for instance $p(t_*):=0$) and define $p'_{\mathrm{reg}}:I\to\mathbb R$ by $p'_{\mathrm{reg}}(t):=p'(t)$ for $t\ne t_*$ and $p'_{\mathrm{reg}}(t_*):=0$. Put $[p]:=p(t_*^+)-p(t_*^-)$ and let $u_p,u_{p'_{\mathrm{reg}}}\in\mathcal D'(I)$ be the associated regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-locally-integrable-function-on-r-n]]): $$u_p(\varphi)=\int_Ip(t)\,\varphi(t)\,d\lambda(t),\qquad u_{p'_{\mathrm{reg}}}(\varphi)=\int_Ip'_{\mathrm{reg}}(t)\,\varphi(t)\,d\lambda(t).$$

Then $p$ and $p'_{\mathrm{reg}}$ are locally integrable on $I$, and

$$(u_p)'=u_{p'_{\mathrm{reg}}}+[p]\,\delta_{t_*}$$

in $\mathcal D'(I)$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]): that is, for every test function $\varphi\in\mathcal D(I)$,

$$-\int_Ip(t)\,\varphi'(t)\,d\lambda(t)=\int_Ip'_{\mathrm{reg}}(t)\,\varphi(t)\,d\lambda(t)+[p]\,\varphi(t_*).$$

Both integrals are over the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R$, and the pairing convention of the two sides is complex-linear in $\varphi$; it therefore suffices that the identity hold for real-valued test functions.
items.strategy: Local integrability from finitely many discontinuities plus the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison; two half-interval integrations by parts of the C1 extensions, assembled with a.e. equality and linearity.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (MIT, 2022): distributional differentiation and the jump of the Heaviside function (the source whose conventions the library distributions use)

David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §1.2, printed p. 2: the variable-mass momentum remark and the caution that a finite force at each point does not by itself determine momentum jumps

items.title: Isolated reciprocal impulse with full-vector restitution: momentum jumps $\pm J$, conservation of total momentum, the restitution solution and the kinetic-energy change $-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from the jump lemma below.
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval with at least two points ([[def-interval]]), let $t_*\in I$, let $m_1,m_2>0$, and let $x_1,x_2:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous on $I$ and twice continuously differentiable on each of the two open intervals $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,\infty)$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Assume the one-sided limits
$$v_i^-:=\lim_{t\uparrow t_*}x_i'(t),\qquad v_i^+:=\lim_{t\downarrow t_*}x_i'(t)\qquad(i=1,2)$$
exist in $\mathbb R^3$. Define $p_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ by $p_i(t):=m_ix_i'(t)$ for $t\ne t_*$ and fix the representative value $p_i(t_*):=0$ ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]). Let $F_1,F_2:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous and let $J\in\mathbb R^3$. The **isolated reciprocal impulse model** at $t_*$ consists of the two requirements:

1. regular dynamics off the impulse: $m_ix_i''(t)=F_i(t)$ for every $t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}$ and $i=1,2$;
2. impulse pairing: for every $\Phi\in C_c^\infty(I;\mathbb R^3)$ — meaning every map whose three components lie in $C_c^\infty(I)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) — $$-\int_I\langle p_1(t),\Phi'(t)\rangle\,d\lambda(t)=\int_I\langle F_1(t),\Phi(t)\rangle\,d\lambda(t)+\langle J,\Phi(t_*)\rangle,$$ $$-\int_I\langle p_2(t),\Phi'(t)\rangle\,d\lambda(t)=\int_I\langle F_2(t),\Phi(t)\rangle\,d\lambda(t)-\langle J,\Phi(t_*)\rangle,$$ with integrals against Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ and the Euclidean inner product $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), using the fixed representative $p_i(t_*)=0$ above.

Under this model, with $M:=m_1+m_2$ and $\mu:=m_1m_2/M$:

**a.** $m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=J$ and $m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)=-J$; consequently the total momentum is continuous across the impulse, $p_1(t_*^+)+p_2(t_*^+)=p_1(t_*^-)+p_2(t_*^-)$.

**b.** Let $e\in[0,1]$ satisfy the **restitution law** $v_2^+-v_1^+=-e(v_2^--v_1^-)$. Then the post-impulse velocities are uniquely determined: with $V:=\frac{m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-}{M}=\frac{m_1v_1^++m_2v_2^+}{M}$, $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}e\,(v_2^--v_1^-),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}e\,(v_2^--v_1^-).$$

**c.** The kinetic-energy change across the impulse is $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2}-\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2}=-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0;$$ in particular $\Delta K=0$ for $e=1$ and $\Delta K=-\frac12\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ for $e=0$.
items.strategy: Apply the scalar jump lemma to each momentum component and compare with the model pairing to get the jumps; solve the linear system for the post-impulse velocities; use the two-body kinetic splitting with the common centre-of-mass velocity.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §1.2-§1.3, printed pp. 2-8: $\mathbf F=\dot{\mathbf p}$ as the primitive balance, together with the caution that the momentum balance of an open (variable-mass) system is not the closed-system statement

Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics, §§1.2-1.3, Eqs. (1.8), (1.30)-(1.38), printed pp. 6-12: isolated-system momentum and pair reciprocity underlying impulse accounting

items.title: Worked impulse and restitution computations and a variable-mass rocket check
items.statement:
Throughout, $e\in\mathbb R^3$ is a unit vector, $\lVert e\rVert_2=1$, for the Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]. All numbers are pure real numbers. For the two collision computations, $v_i^-$ and $v_i^+$ denote pre- and post-collision vectors. Given positive masses and $e_r\in[0,1]$, require only the finite algebraic relations

$$m_1v_1^++m_2v_2^+=m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-,\qquad v_2^+-v_1^+=-e_r(v_2^--v_1^-).$$

Define $J:=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)$ and

$$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2-m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2-m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2}.$$

The two cases below solve these relations uniquely and compute $J$ and $\Delta K$ directly. No distributional jump theorem or choice assumption is used in these finite calculations.

**(i) Equal masses, half-elastic impulse.** Take $m_1=m_2=1$, approach velocities $v_1^-=1\,e$, $v_2^-=-1\,e$ and restitution coefficient $e_r=\frac12$. Then the unique post-collision vectors, impulse and kinetic-energy change are

$$v_1^+=-\tfrac12\,e,\qquad v_2^+=\tfrac12\,e,\qquad J=-\tfrac32\,e,\qquad \Delta K=-\tfrac34 .$$

**(ii) Elastic impulse with unequal masses.** Take $m_1=1$, $m_2=3$, $v_1^-=2\,e$, $v_2^-=0$ and $e_r=1$. Then

$$v_1^+=-1\,e,\qquad v_2^+=1\,e,\qquad J=-3\,e,\qquad \Delta K=0 .$$

**(iii) Rocket check.** On $I=[0,1]$ take $m(t):=2-t$, $v(t):=\ln\!\bigl(\frac{2}{2-t}\bigr)e$, $F\equiv0$, $r_{\mathrm{in}}\equiv0$, $r_{\mathrm{out}}\equiv1$, $w_{\mathrm{in}}\equiv0$, $w_{\mathrm{out}}(t):=v(t)-u_e\,e$ with $u_e:=1$. Then the two material balance identities of [[thm-cm-variable-mass-momentum-balance]] hold, the derived law reads $m(t)v'(t)=1\cdot e$, and $v(1)=\ln(2)\,e$. The naive closed-system reading $(mv)'=F\equiv0$ would instead force $v\equiv v(0)=0$ on $I$, which does not satisfy the material balance; the two readings differ as soon as $t>0$.
items.strategy: Solve finite momentum and restitution equations uniquely and evaluate kinetic differences directly, without the distributional jump theorem or choice assumption; differentiate the rocket functions on all [0,1] and compare the naive candidate with fixed outflow data.

references.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), §§1.2-1.3, printed pp. 2-8: momentum balances and the variable-mass caution
Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics, §3.4, Eqs. (3.30)-(3.37), printed pp. 40-42: centre-of-mass and reduced-mass kinetic splitting used in the collision arithmetic

items.title: Breakdown versus trapping: the blow-up of $x'=x^2$ and the global trapped solution of $x'=-x^2$
items.statement:
Let $D:=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$. For $z\in\mathbb R$ define $G_+(z):=z^2$ and $G_-(z):=-z^2$, and define the autonomous vector fields $F_\pm:D\to\mathbb R$ by $F_\pm(t,z):=G_\pm(z)$. Their continuity and local Lipschitz property in the state variable are verified below.

**(i) Finite-time breakdown despite a pointwise-finite vector field.** The function $x_+:[0,1)\to\mathbb R$, $x_+(t):=\frac{1}{1-t}$, solves $x'(t)=F_+(t,x_+(t))$ with $x(0)=1$ on $[0,1)$, and no solution of this initial value problem extends past $b=1$. For every compact $K\subseteq D$ and every $\eta>0$ there is $t\in(1-\eta,1)$ with $(t,x_+(t))\notin K$: the graph leaves every compact subset of $D$ as $t\uparrow1$. The compact-containment hypothesis of [[thm-cm-compact-continuation-for-locally-lipschitz-odes]] fails here, and its escape consequence [[cor-cm-finite-time-breakdown-requires-escape]] is witnessed explicitly.

**(ii) Trapping forces continuation.** The function $x_-:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$, $x_-(t):=\frac{1}{1+t}$, solves $x'(t)=F_-(t,x_-(t))$ with $x(0)=1$, and its values lie in the compact set $K_0:=[0,1]\subseteq\mathbb R$. For each finite $b>0$, its restriction to $[0,b)$ is trapped in $K_0$, so clause 2 of [[cor-cm-finite-time-breakdown-requires-escape]] extends it past $b$; thus no finite right endpoint is nonextendable, and the displayed formula supplies a global extension on $[0,\infty)$.

Both fields are the same polynomial expression up to sign, so (i) and (ii) exhibit the continuation criterion of [[thm-cm-compact-continuation-for-locally-lipschitz-odes]] as a statement about compact trapping, not about pointwise finiteness of the vector field.
items.strategy: Verify the closed forms by the quotient rule and local Lipschitz continuity of the fields by the mean value inequality; prove non-extendability by uniqueness plus boundedness of a continuous solution on [0,1]; verify trapping directly.
